channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Governo Lula envia nova remessa de ajuda humanitária a Cuba
item.description: The Lula government sent 48 tons of powdered milk to Cuba in two shipments via the Brazilian Air Force, coordinated by the ABC and supported by Conab, marking Brazil’s third humanitarian aid mission to the island in 2026 amid its supply crisis. The operation was agreed upon in a July 9 ministerial meeting and focuses on non-perishable food, explicitly ruling out energy aid due to U.S. sanctions risks on Petrobras if it supplied fuel to Cuba.

item.title: Bolsonaro copia carta de Lula, mas não apaga crimes que o tiraram das redes
item.description: From detention in Brasília, Jair Bolsonaro released a 'Letter to Brazilians' mimicking the title and format of Lula's 2018 'Letter to the Brazilian People', naming his eldest son as his presidential candidate for 2026. The move comes while he remains ineligible due to convictions for abuse of power and misuse of media, which bar him from running in elections.

item.title: Decisão de Moraes vai aumentar intenções de voto de Flávio Bolsonaro, diz presidente do PL
item.description: PL party president Valdemar Costa Neto claims that Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to ban Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father for 90 days after the senator shared a letter from the ex-president endorsing his candidacy will increase Flávio's voter intentions for the 2026 presidential race. He argues the move, seen as an attempt to politically silence the Bolsonaro family, will trigger a backlash reflected in upcoming polls. Flávio Bolsonaro's lawyers denounced the decision as unconstitutional, violating penal execution law, the Statute of the Bar, and the Constitution by denying familial visitation rights.

item.title: As possíveis implicações contra Flávio após carta de Bolsonaro
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes has ordered the Electoral Attorney General's Office to rule on a video by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in which he read a letter from former President Jair Bolsonaro declaring him his 'spokesperson', considered potential premature electoral propaganda. While there is no risk of ineligibility or criminal punishment, the PGE may impose a fine between R$5,000 and R$25,000 if it finds the content exceeds legal limits. The video was released amid a family crisis after Michelle Bolsonaro accused Flávio of humiliating her, damaging his standing among female voters.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil deixará de ser “exportador de matéria-prima”
item.description: President Lula stated that Brazil will no longer export raw materials and advocated for the domestic industrialization of critical minerals and rare earths, emphasizing the need to add value to natural resources. He stressed that exploration of these minerals must occur within the country, citing historical examples of gold, silver, and iron, and highlighted the importance of the Armed Forces in protecting national sovereignty, including borders, oil, and underground wealth.

item.title: Entenda como funciona o sistema eletrônico das votações no Senado
item.description: The Federal Senate has its own electronic voting system, in use since 2006 in the Plenary and 2016 in committees, which was modernized in 2026 with new touchscreens, credential and biometric authentication, and integration with the Chamber of Deputies for joint votes. The system ensures security, secrecy, and accurate vote counting in accordance with the Constitution, and was specifically designed for parliamentary voting — not the same system used in general elections by Brazil's Electoral Justice.

item.title: El juez prohíbe que Flávio Bolsonaro visite a su padre durante la campaña electoral
item.description: Supreme Federal Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has barred Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving house arrest in Brasília, after Flávio shared on social media a letter from his father calling for unity on the right around his candidacy. The judge ruled the act violated precautionary measures, as Bolsonaro is prohibited from communicating with the outside world, either directly or through intermediaries.

item.title: Bolsonaristas criticam decisão de Moraes citando cartas de Lula durante prisão
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) criticized Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to suspend Jair Bolsonaro's visits for 90 days, drawing parallels to letters written by Lula during his imprisonment from 2018 to 2019. They argue the measure is inconsistent, as Lula also wrote letters while incarcerated without facing similar restrictions. The controversy unfolds ahead of the 2026 elections, with Bolsonaro as a pre-candidate.

item.title: Bolsonaro pode perder o benefício da prisão domiciliar se for comprovado que sabia da divulgação da carta do filho, dizem advogados
item.description: Legal experts say former President Jair Bolsonaro could lose his house arrest benefit if the Supreme Court proves he knew of and consented to the dissemination of a letter by his son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, which would constitute a violation of the conditions of his humanitarian house arrest.

item.title: Suspensão de visitas ao pai é inconstitucional, diz defesa de Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's defense claims that Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to bar the senator from visiting his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days, is illegal and unconstitutional. The ban followed Flávio's social media posting of a letter signed by Bolsonaro, which Moraes deemed a violation of a judicial order restricting the ex-president's social media use via third parties. The defense argues the measure violates constitutional rights, the Penal Execution Law, and the Advocacy Statute, particularly because Flávio also serves as his father's lawyer.

item.title: TSE atualiza e-Título e aplicativo agora terá pagamento Pix
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has updated the e-Título app with new features, including the ability to pay electoral debts via Pix, document validation via QR code, simplified absence justification, volunteer poll worker unregistration, integrated 'Boletim na Mão', native issuance of party affiliation certificates, and secure authentication token generation requiring facial recognition. The updates aim to increase voter autonomy and streamline election-day identification.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil não quer guerra, mas precisa estar preparado
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil does not seek war but must be prepared to defend its sovereignty, emphasizing the need to protect resources such as rare earths and oil. He advocated for strengthening the national defense industry during the presentation of the first ethanol-powered turbine developed by the IAE. However, Poder360 data shows a 35.5% decline in Operation Ágata during his first three years in office compared to the Bolsonaro administration.

item.title: Girão destaca manifestação de Cármen Lúcia sobre Conselho de Ética
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE) highlighted that Minister Cármen Lúcia of the STF ordered the Senate to provide information within ten days regarding a mandamus filed by his party to install the Ethics and Parliamentary Decorum Council. He also criticized the Senate's restriction on citizen comments in its institutional posts on X during the electoral period, arguing it undermines public participation in legislative debates.

item.title: O principal problema do Brasil segundo eleitores a favor de Lula e de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A Nexus poll shows that among Lula supporters, 31% cite violence as Brazil's main problem, followed by public health at 25%. Among Flávio Bolsonaro supporters, 33% identify corruption as the top issue, and 29% mention violence. Overall, public security/violence is the leading concern (29%), followed by corruption (24%) and public health (23%).

item.title: Valdemar aposta em crescimento de Flávio após restrição imposta por Moraes
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the Liberal Party (PL), believes that the ban imposed by Minister Alexandre de Moraes preventing Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting former president Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days will boost the pre-candidate in the polls. He argues that the restriction will only increase Flávio’s visibility and support.

item.title: Lula diz que Irã “nem tinha competência” para fazer arma nuclear
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Iran lacked the capability to develop nuclear weapons and that U.S. claims about an Iranian nuclear arsenal are false, drawing a parallel to the 2003 Iraq invasion based on unverified allegations of weapons of mass destruction. He also accused the U.S. of practicing 'piracy' by seeking control of the Strait of Hormuz and imposing a 20% fee on maritime traffic, which has contributed to escalating tensions and a surge in oil prices.

item.title: Damares nega rompimento com Flávio e reclama de ataques entre aliados
item.description: Senator Damares Alves denied breaking with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro but criticized internal attacks among right-wing allies, calling them 'friendly fire'. She reaffirmed her support for the candidate chosen by Jair Bolsonaro and questioned who finances the defamation campaigns against conservatives, emphasizing her loyalty to Michelle Bolsonaro.

item.title: Moraes impõe ‘freio inibitório’ e isola Bolsonaro para impedir papel de cabo eleitoral
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes barred Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting former President Jair Bolsonaro for the next 90 days to prevent the ex-president from exerting political influence in his son's electoral campaign. The measure reinforces a prior 'inhibitory brake,' banning any external communication aimed at mobilizing supporters, including letters or third-party messages. While Bolsonaro's allies claim persecution, Moraes and other justices argue that releasing him could inflame the political climate and boost the 'Zero Um' campaign.

item.title: Pesquisa mostra ponto de fragilidade interna da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows that the rift between Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro is negatively impacting perceptions of the senator’s presidential candidacy, with 27% of respondents saying the impact will be large and 19% small. Political scientist Leonardo Barreto notes the effect is stronger among independent voters and Bolsonaro sympathizers — a key swing group in the election. Despite Flávio’s efforts to assert himself as Jair Bolsonaro’s official spokesperson, including using a handwritten letter from the former president, internal resistance remains, particularly among conservative women and evangelical voters, signaling a division within the Bolsonarist base.

item.title: Alcolumbre se irrita com governo Lula após ofensiva da PF, e PT inicia campanha #AprovaSenado
item.description: The PT launched the #AprovaSenado campaign to pressure Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to vote on the PEC ending the 6x1 work schedule by May 16, but relations between Lula's government and Congress deteriorated after PF operations blocked parliamentary amendments tied to Centrão allies like Valdemar Costa Neto and Eduardo Cunha. Alcolumbre and Chamber President Hugo Motta blame STF Minister Flávio Dino, appointed by Lula, for the blockage, causing private irritation in the Senate and delaying key government agendas.

item.title: Damares diz que ‘ainda’ apoia Flávio e defende Michelle: ‘não trai, não mente, não se corrompe’
item.description: Senator Damares Alves reaffirmed her support for Flávio Bolsonaro as the pre-candidate endorsed by Jair Bolsonaro, despite criticism that she is not campaigning enough for him. She also publicly defended Michelle Bolsonaro, describing her as a dignified, just, and honest woman who does not lie, betray, or become corrupt, and emphasized that Michelle is alone in her political struggle within the Bolsonaro clan. The tension between Michelle and Flávio reflects an internal struggle over Jair Bolsonaro’s political legacy, with Michelle seeking her own political space while Flávio is positioned as the official heir.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: Cresce a chance da terceira via
item.description: A poll discussed on Papo Antagonista shows that the share of Brazilians preferring a candidate not backed by Lula or Jair Bolsonaro rose from 11% in March to 27% in the May 13 survey, signaling a notable growth of the third way in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Michelle demonstrou preocupação com carta de Bolsonaro a Flávio e relatou a aliadas de revés no STF
item.description: Former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro expressed concern over a letter written by Jair Bolsonaro to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, after Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes banned communication between them for 90 days, dealing a setback to the PL’s presidential campaign. Michelle fears the letter’s disclosure could lead to the revocation of Jair Bolsonaro’s house arrest, endangering his health, and had previously criticized Flávio publicly for alleged disrespect. The ruling also requires Jair Bolsonaro’s defense to clarify whether he knew the letter would be shared on his son’s social media and forwards the case to the electoral prosecutor for investigation of potential premature electoral propaganda.

item.title: ‘Aloprados’: Damares Alves sai em defesa de Michelle Bolsonaro e critica ataques
item.description: Senator Damares Alves (PL-DF) defended former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro against attacks originating from within the right-wing political sphere, alleging that former party aides are spreading rumors about Michelle planning to create a new party to destabilize Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy. She claimed Michelle is being targeted by an organized, possibly funded campaign and questioned who is financing the attacks, emphasizing Michelle's loyalty, honesty, and integrity.

item.title: Proibição de visita de Flávio a Bolsonaro é interferência no jogo político, diz Marinho
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), campaign coordinator for Flávio Bolsonaro, criticized the decision by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes to prohibit Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting former President Jair Bolsonaro, calling it political interference. He argued the measure violates the right to defense and the free exercise of political activity.

item.title: TSE debate impacto da IA e combate a deepfakes em fórum global na Índia
item.description: The TSE participated in the Fundamental Course on Artificial Intelligence and Elections in India from July 6–10, representing Brazil in sharing best practices on AI use and combating technological disinformation. Representative Leonardo Oliveira from the DAE presented the evolution of Brazil’s electronic voting system and strategies to counter deepfakes and tech-driven disinformation. The event reinforced the TSE’s regulatory role in the global electoral management landscape.

item.title: Dino suspende regra que dispensava eleição para presidência da Aleam
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino suspended the effects of a rule from the Amazonas Legislative Assembly (Aleam) that allowed the vice-president to assume the presidency permanently in case of vacancy without a new election. The decision ensures that the presidency of Aleam is filled through a direct vote by deputies, reinforcing democratic principles and internal legality of the state legislature.

item.title: Moraes diz que Flávio é reincidente em descumprir decisões
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes stated that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro is a repeat offender in violating judicial rulings, having used a visit to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, to disseminate a politically charged letter barred by court order. The ruling suspended visits for 90 days, required the defense to clarify whether Jair Bolsonaro knew of the publication, and referred the material to the Electoral Attorney General's Office for evaluation of potential premature electoral propaganda.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio dizem que decisão de Moraes interfere no jogo político e torcem por efeito rebote
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro believe that Alexandre de Moraes’ decision to suspend his visits to jailed father Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days may backfire, generating sympathy among Bolsonarist voters and reinforcing claims of political persecution. They argue the measure will not disrupt pre-campaign organizing, as communication can continue through lawyers and strategies were already set. They hope the episode will boost Flávio’s polling by reviving debates on liberty and institutional balance.

item.title: Moro cita Lula e critica Moraes por suspender visitas de Flávio a Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro (PL-PR) criticized Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to suspend visits from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to jailed former President Jair Bolsonaro, claiming it violates correspondence rights and lacks proportionality. Moro compared the situation to Lula's imprisonment from 2018 to 2019, when Lula received 572 visits — including 21 from Fernando Haddad — and stated he never sought to restrict such rights during his time as a federal judge.

item.title: Damares diz que Michelle está "aflita" após decisão de Moraes
item.description: Senator Damares Alves said Michelle Bolsonaro is distressed following a decision by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, which suspended Flávio Bolsonaro's visitation rights to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days. Michelle allegedly remains committed to complying with the precautionary measures imposed on the former president and feels virtually confined with him. The ruling came after Flávio shared a letter of support from Jair for his presidential campaign, potentially violating the social media ban imposed in March.

item.title: Valdemar: veto à visita de Flávio a Bolsonaro o fará subir nas pesquisas
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL party, claims that Alexandre de Moraes' ban on Flávio Bolsonaro visiting Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days will boost the senator's polling numbers. The measure, which prevents contact before the first round of the 2026 elections, is seen as a factor that will increase Flávio's visibility and support as the party's presidential pre-candidate.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio criticam decisão de Moraes e comparam à prisão de Lula
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro criticized a decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes that barred the senator from visiting his father, Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days over the dissemination of a letter. Senator Rogério Marinho argued the measure is disproportionate, authoritarian, and reflects a double standard, citing Lula’s ability to communicate while imprisoned in 2018. The restriction is seen as harmful to Flávio’s pre-campaign and as political interference.

item.title: Mulheres pedem aprovação imediata do projeto que torna a misoginia crime
item.description: Activists and experts urged the immediate approval of Bill 896/2023, which criminalizes misogyny in Brazil, equating it with racism and prescribing two to five years in prison. The bill, already passed in the Senate, aims to combat gender-based violence rooted in structural hatred of women. Supporters argue its passage is vital to changing the nation’s civilizational model and stopping the production of femicides.

item.title: Moro critica decisão de Moraes que proibiu Flávio de visitar Bolsonaro: 'falta legalidade'
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro criticized Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the STF for banning Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting former President Jair Bolsonaro, citing a lack of proportionality and legality in the decision. Moro, former judge of Operation Car Wash, argued that the measure violates fundamental principles of the rule of law.

item.title: Defesa de Flávio diz que suspensão das visitas ao pai fere direito como advogado
item.description: The defense of Flávio Bolsonaro claims that the suspension of visits to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, ordered by Minister Alexandre de Moraes, is illegal and unconstitutional, as it violates the lawyer's right to communicate with his client. The measure followed Flávio's disclosure of a letter from Jair Bolsonaro on social media, which Moraes deemed a breach of judicial order. The defense argues the ban infringes on the Penal Execution Law, the Statute of the OAB, and the Constitution.

item.title: Católicos e evangélicos divergem sobre capacidade de candidatos pelos direitos das mulheres, aponta pesquisa
item.description: Catholics and evangelicals show divergent views on which presidential candidate is best equipped to guarantee women's rights, according to a BTG/Nexus poll. While 56% of Catholics favor Lula, only 36% choose Flávio Bolsonaro; among evangelicals, 50% prefer Flávio Bolsonaro and 41% trust Lula. The margin of error is 2 percentage points at a 95% confidence level.

item.title: O Antagonista e G4 promovem sabatina com pré-candidatos à Presidência
item.description: O Antagonista and G4, one of Brazil's largest executive education and corporate solutions companies, are hosting a candidate forum on August 4 featuring the main pre-candidates for the 2026 presidential election. Invited participants include President Lula (PT), Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), and former governors Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Romeu Zema. The event aims to discuss candidates' proposals and positions ahead of the election.

item.title: Os números da pesquisa BTG/Nexus que animaram Renan Santos
item.description: Allies of Renan Santos celebrated the rise in voters rejecting both Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, from 9% to 11%, and the increase in those wanting a president not backed by either, from 21% to 27%. Renan celebrated being in third place with low rejection and high growth potential, stating that as he becomes better known, he could reach the runoff and defeat Lula.

item.title: Novo e-Título: baixe o app, conheça suas funções e exerça a cidadania nas Eleições 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has updated the e-Título app, the official digital platform for voter ID access, adding features such as PIX-based debt payment, real-time certificate issuance, and enhanced security tools. The app aims to centralize electoral services, streamline voter identification on election day, and promote full civic participation, urging early download to prevent virtual congestion.

item.title: A crítica de Lula depois de apenas um jogador da Seleção voltar ao Brasil
item.description: President Lula criticized the low number of Brazilian national team players who returned to Brazil after the team's elimination by Norway in the Round of 16 of the 2026 World Cup, noting that only Danilo of Flamengo had come back. He made the remarks in a lighthearted tone during an event at the Mauá Institute of Technology in São Paulo, where he also praised a student-built robot, comparing it to Mbappé and Haaland. Lula jokingly suggested that Ancelotti should sign the robot to help Brazil win future World Cups.

item.title: Bolsonaristas criticam Moraes após suspensão das visitas de Flávio ao pai e lembram carta escrita por Lula na prisão
item.description: Bolsonarista allies criticized Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to suspend Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's visits to former President Jair Bolsonaro, claiming Flávio violated a ban by using the meeting to obtain a document later shared on social media. In response, supporters recalled a 2018 letter written by Lula while imprisoned, which endorsed Fernando Haddad's candidacy, arguing that restricting visits is politically motivated and undermines fundamental rights.

item.title: Para conter greve dos caminhoneiros, governo e oposição fecham acordo para votar MP do Frete
item.description: Government and opposition lawmakers reached an agreement with truckers' representatives to vote on the Freight MP this week, including textual adjustments and signaling presidential vetoes by Lula on provisions such as amnesty for fines related to post-2022 election protests. The deal, led by Senate leader Teresa Leitão and House leader Randolfe Rodrigues, with opposition senators Tereza Cristina and Jaime Bagatolli, aims to prevent a repeat of the 2018 truckers' strike crisis.

item.title: “Decisão de Moraes é ilegal”, diz pré-campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The lawyer for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign, Tracy Reinaldet, stated that the decision by Minister Alexandre de Moraes to prohibit the senator from visiting his father for 90 days is illegal and unconstitutional. The statement was made in an official note released on Thursday afternoon.

item.title: Defesa de Flávio Bolsonaro diz que decisão de Moraes de suspender visitas ao pai desrespeita Constituição
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's defense claims that the suspension of visits to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, ordered by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, violates the Constitution and the rights of incarcerated individuals to receive family visits and communicate with the outside world, as well as the lawyer's right to communicate with their client. The measure followed Flávio reading a letter from his father on social media, which Moraes deemed a violation of the ban on the former president using social media directly or through third parties. The 90-day suspension prevents contact until mid-October, after the first round of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Lula diz que guerra “provocada pelos EUA” encarece comida no Brasil
item.description: President Lula stated that the Iran war, provoked by the U.S., is raising food prices in Brazil due to increased fuel costs. He defended a 12% tax on oil exports as a way to subsidize domestic fuel and curb inflation. Speaking at the Mauá Institute of Technology, he also stressed the need for energy transition, supported raising biodiesel blend to B17, and criticized Donald Trump’s stance on climate change.

item.title: O que Michelle achou da decisão de Moraes proibir Flávio Bolsonaro de visitar o pai?
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to ban Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father, Jair Bolsonaro, for three months has drawn criticism that the justice is acting out of personal persecution against the Bolsonaro family, drawing a parallel to Fernando Haddad's visits to Lula in prison in 2018, which were not punished. The text argues that Moraes has lost credibility due to controversies like the Banco Master case and should recuse himself in matters involving the Bolsonaro family to promote national stability.

item.title: Ego de Alexandre de Moraes vai entregar eleição para Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The article claims that TSE President Alexandre de Moraes is letting his ego shape judicial decisions, which could inadvertently benefit Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 elections. It argues that judicial rulings are being weaponized to create a persecution narrative that strengthens Bolsonaro’s political position.

item.title: Governo Lula tenta acordo com oposição para votar MP da tabela do frete em meio a pressão de caminhoneiros
item.description: The Lula government is seeking an agreement with the opposition to vote in the Senate on the freight table MP, which expands ANTT’s powers to enforce the minimum freight price and includes a planned veto on pardoning fines for truckers involved in 2022 blockades. The measure must be approved by Thursday to avoid expiration, and government leader Randolfe Rodrigues confirmed the minimum price is retained in the proposal but without a fixed value due to constitutional limitations. The meeting included opposition senators and presidential representatives to address disagreements on the Ciot and minimum floor.

item.title: Moro compara caso de Lula à restrição de visitas de Flávio a Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro criticized Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to ban Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting former President Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days. Moro compared the restriction to the judicial treatment of former President Lula during his imprisonment, arguing both cases represent political use of judicial power.
